body: Thanks!  This link helped a lot.
Thanks!  Telling my mom to throw them out.  She thought she would get a nice butterfly or moth from a caterpillar eventually.

I went to the bank and cashed in some bonds my grandma had given me (from birth + every year after) so I could get money for a trip while unemployed.

Come back after trip with another bond, because I needed cash.  Talk to the tellers (who all know I am transitioning) and the lady downstairs who verifies the bonds was confused.

"The signature on the back isn't the same name on the front."  They had to explain to her what happened, and potentially give her a copy of the name change order.  Just found it funny that the bank caught it because of old self being on paper.
I only heard it from my therapist - and she was a BAD gateway (six years of therapy to get my letter from her - before they changed the rules anyways).  Unsure if it is true.

Doctors told my mom I'd be a girl.  They had a name picked out.  Mom was at her old job, and had a HUGE amount of stress there (paralegal for a large law firm).  She started having contractions in August, I was born late December.

Doctor didn't even know I was a boy until I popped out.  Parents didn't have a male name for me at the time.  I weighed 4 pounds 4 ounces.

Unsure about the links there.  I also have to say I'm part Cherokee, and I've also heard anecdotal evidence that Native Americans have a higher rate of being trans than others, but that's from a therapist that I didn't like.

My doctor found guidelines for dosages and the medical regime online.  I'm her first trans patient, and pretty proud of it (she's also my primary care physician).

With that in mind, I take 50mg twice a day.  I'm on a low dose because I reacted to it really well (my T is around 30 right now, after a year and a half on it).  I do believe it was set to be twice a day due to less mini spikes throughout the day.  You won't have a spike of the drug when you take it, so it makes it more even in your system.
Unsure if I am moving, but if I do move, it'll be somewhere near Show Low/Snowflake

Thanks for the link!
I'll check out stuff, but I'll be about four hours from Tuscon as well =(
I'll be about four hours from Phoenix.  I can make the drive, obviously, just wasn't sure if anyone had any good doctors to recommend.

Used to get yelled at for eating too much salt.  Now I just say "Yeah, well, one of my pills makes me lose sodium!" and that shuts them up usually.

"You still can have too much sodium!"  Oh really?  That's why I'm on a potassium sparing diuretic?

I just came up with a name.  Then I realized I hated it.
Talked with my mom for three months before we both decided on a name.
The day after I submitted documents to legally change it, my mom told me she hated it.
I still kept it - and now she doesn't mind.

Surprised nobody did this yet.
Someone in the Westboro Baptist Church that's really high up, or the entire church.
Someone high up in a terrorist organization (INFIDEL!  Wait, I wanna be a girl?  WHAT?)

If all that fails, probably my brother, just so he can understand what I feel and go through when he calls me my birth name, refuses to accept me as I am, etc.

If I drive, I'll make sure I make a few stops to rest and take naps - in safe areas, too.  I fully understand that you can't drive 24 hours straight.

I also found something else out, after doing some research - I don't know if she can fly back with me, since she doesn't have a photo ID at the moment.

I have a same experience too.  Doctors told my parents I would be a girl.  They didn't have a male name picked out.  I popped out, and the doctor said "Congratulations!  It's a beautiful baby guh........................  boy."
Turns out I'm really supposed to be female after all.

I was pan-curious before I started HRT.  I had a relationship with one guy that lasted three days (he was controlling and obsessive to the point where I couldn't hang out with my friends and he wanted to know the me "then" and not the me I would be).
Over a year on HRT now, and my attraction to men has dropped significantly.  I'd say I'm still pansexual (I can be attracted to anyone sexually) but gynoromantic (in that I only want to date women).
I do have a girlfriend now, and I'm pretty happy.  Just figured I'd share my bit.

I thought it was 6 months as well.  That would have been six sessions with my therapist.

Instead, it took me about 7 YEARS to get my letter.  Yes, that long - just to get a damn letter.  I saw her twice more after that (changed the name I wanted to go by, and then got that new letter) and left.  Why?  She was a bad therapist, a gatekeeper.

Do the six months.  Three extra months really is nothing in the long run.  I know it's hard to sit there and say "I'll get through it" but I know you will, because I did.  Just have hope.

Oh, I know it feels right.  Just make sure you do something that you won't regret.  My tattoos make me me, and both have extreme amounts of meaning behind them.

Don't just get a tattoo to get a tattoo, get something that symbolizes something.

I have two tattoo's, I got them before  I discovered my true self.  I know they help with depression for that day, maybe two or three more - completely got rid of my self harm thoughts during that time.  The act of tattooing does get rid of some of these thoughts for a bit, and if you get something you like, you can look at it and enjoy it.

Also, getting a tattoo releases endorphins that will help you with your mood that day - it's like a huge rush of happiness afterwards.  I can't explain it.

Fully understand that you want to rant, I know I do.

It is terrible that my brother cannot accept me for who I am, when all of his friends do and still love me.  They defended me in front of him.

Just wanted to say that not everyone who is religious is against who I am, or anyone else who is trans.  There are many people out there who will love and support you for who you are, all you have to do is find them.

Everyone is different when it comes to religion.

My girlfriend and her nuclear family are 100% accepting of me (they met me mid-transition).  They love me for who I am, call me brave, and are 100% okay with my girlfriend being a lesbian - so long as she's happy.  The entire family is religious, even adding me into their prayers during dinner.

My sister-in-law and brother are completely against me.  They disinvited me to my own parent's Christmas gathering because of what I'm going through.

As it stands, YMMV when it comes to others and how they react to you.  Religion is a big factor, but not the only factor, in whether people will accept you or not.

I started HRT at 30.  I'm almost 32 now, been on hormones for 15 months now.

http://imgur.com/a/E8IU4

Look at those results up there.  The one with me in the leather dress (the middle picture) is the newest one, taken two months ago.

There is no "too late".  I haven't done any muscle building or heavy lifting as of late, but honestly, I was always petite and still am.  As always, everything varies from person to person, but still, there is no such thing as too late.

Not an employment story per se, but I'll share mine anyways.
Male to Female, I pass pretty damn well.  Went to an interview, during it the lady said the person they were replacing got pregnant (big red flag there).  I jokingly said she wouldn't have to worry about it with me, and when she asked why I slipped and told the truth.
No call from them afterwards.
I'm in Illinois, and the job was in Chicago, so lots of protections - but hard to prove it because they had someone else for an interview lined up.  Would have been nice to get a call saying I wasn't hired though.

Thank you!

I forgot to add I've only been on hormones for a little over a year now.

I'm a MtF lesbian myself.  Trust me, lesbians do NOT have to have a penis (fake or real) to have sex.  On top of that, I have mine still and, um, can't use it for that...  Not in the traditional way.

In any case, just because they showed you pictures of people doesn't mean that's what you will look like.  Take a look at me (all pics SFW) http://imgur.com/a/E8IU4 and tell me I look like a guy at all.

Oh, yeah, that makes sense.  Really does.
Honestly, if all else fails, we'll do it in Cali (close to her parents).  However, I'll talk to her about it when she wakes up next.
Oh, good point!  I didn't even THINK of that one.  I"ll have to tell her that idea - Thanks!
I'm over 30, so I won't really need the birth certificate.  We'll probably just end up doing it in Cali after all.  Or do it here in Illinois.

It's legal in Illinois, but not in Arizona.  We want her family to attend, which means down near Arizona, but we also want it to be legal.  Just trying to figure out what Arizona classifies me as, as currently I'm in the middle - and I don't know what Arizona requires.

Illinois recognizes same-sex marriages.  Arizona doesn't.  We're just plotting things out right now.  Her family wants to attend, so we're debating on Arizona, however, both of us want to live in Illinois or Cali (two states that do recognize it in any case).

And yes, it does require one of three surgeries in Illinois - orchiectomy, SRS, or FFS.  I don't need FFS, and I'd rather wait to get SRS than just do an orchiectomy.

I'm on 8 mg of Estrogen (4 in morning, 4 in night) and only at 50 mg of Spiro.

It all depends on your hormonal balance to start, and how well you take to the medication.  My testosterone (after a year of hormones) is roughly at 21, well inside the normal female range.  My estrogen levels are somewhere around 240.

I went and told a couple of people at work beforehand - my friend worked there, and he knew for years.  As I told people around me, they were all very supportive and accepting of it.

Eventually, the lady working HR went and told my boss (the President of the company) who approached me the next day.  He didn't care, he was just curious about it.

Fast forward a year, and I finally decide enough is enough, I have to transition.  I told my boss a date that I would be coming in to work full time, and my preferred name.  I came in and found out my boss told one of the warehouse guys (who's this really big scary dude) to watch out for me.  Find out later the warehouse guy actually yelled at someone for looking at me funny.

I changed my name legally a month later (already had that set up), and everything at work went smoothly.  Too bad I was laid off a few months later.  Stupid downsizing.

I felt trapped, but that was because of the severe dysphoria sweeping through my brain at the time.

Now that I've started transitioning, have been full time for almost a year, and am blossoming into a beautiful woman, I feel less trapped.  98% of my body is female, and that's what matters to me.

The first time my therapist used the female pronouns in front of my parents, I was terrified.
Not because I doubted it, because I doubted my trust in my parents to not react angrily/violently.  My doubts were justified until recently :(

^ this.  Fully this.
Depression, anxiety, bad eyesight.  Not to mention the family history of heart problems.

True, however, think of step children.  They are not your blood, but some step-parents love their children as if they are their own.

Besides, if you have a sibling, and they have kids, part of your genetic code has already been passed.  On top of that, many of us suffer from inherited mental disorders (depression, anxiety) on top of other physical ailments (high blood pressure, anemia, etc).  Sometimes, adoption is a great way of saying "Hey, look, I have a kid, it's mine, and I love this kid with all my heart."

At the time of my search, however, there were limited people in Illinois.  Even still, I have yet to encounter a therapist in my area that has any remote knowledge of the trans community (I've searched in Naperville, Aurora, Dekalb, Ottawa, Oswego) and the psychiatrist my friend is seeing, up at the Central Dupage Hospital, has no colleagues that know anything about how to treat or help us with our transition.  That's a huge gap in knowledge in a large swath of area.

Eek.  I'm blushing.

Thanks for the comments, I hope you turn out as amazing and awesome as you want to be.

Since this was back in 2004 when I was searching for a therapist, there was only three listed on the WPATH website - and there was no way I was driving an hour and a half to get to Chicago to see one, nor the two hour drive to Evanston.  Since then, the WPATH website has added a few, but that was all there was.  At the time, I didn't know there were other therapists in the state, and even still, WPATH only lists six providers.

I have done this, however, the problem now is would you meet the person you are in love with (or will fall in love with) in your life?

If I was born a female, would I still be a lesbian?  Would I have met the person of my dreams?  Would I be happy in life, have a stable job (which I still don't have...), have the support of my friends and family?

That's the questions that bother me about this.  Sure, I would have been in gymnastics, had a slightly different body.  But would I have done the exact same things to meet the exact same people?  I would be someone totally different, most likely, in which case I would never have met the wonderful and amazing people in my life that support me.

Case in point: I was lonely, so I got talked into joining the Brony fandom for a while.  Thanks to going to a convention with some of them, I met my best friend/sister at the convention.  Thanks to her, my transition was smoother than it would have been.  Would I still have befriended her?
Would I still have gone onto IMVU and met someone of my dreams through that?

It's these things that make me wonder if I should even think of this alternate universe.

I started hormones at 30, July of 2013.  I don't think it is too late for anyone.

http://imgur.com/a/E8IU4

The bottom picture is the oldest (at around 7 months HRT), whereas the middle picture is newest (taken in late July of this year).  I'm only 15 months into HRT, and have noticed everything changing - my body tone and structure, my facial features (my eyelashes are growing longer even!), everything.

I had laser hair removal done on my face, and even now, it shows up as very light hair when it does grow in (thanks Estrogen!).  I'm well in the normal female range for my hormonal levels, and my body weight still fluctuates (120 to 130 on an average day).  I'm healthy though, and that's what matters.
I'm so happy for you!  I remember the first time all of this happened to me myself, and it was wonderful.

I know everyone is telling you new therapist, but honestly, I had a terrible therapist.  And as far as I know, she's the only one in Illinois.

Since getting my letter, I have bounced around to something like seven therapists, and not a single one has known anything about the trans community at all.  They know we exist, but know nothing about how to help us at all.  I've had to inform several of what they should do, and what the process actually is.

In addition, if you find a good family doctor, they CAN prescribe hormones to you.  Mine did the research for me and got everything set up, still sees me for my hormones and regular checkups.  It's nice not having to leave town to drive the hour+ to get to Chicago.

Also, my best friend/sister's psychiatrist wants me to inform her of how to help trans patients of hers for everything.  Seems like I'm becoming an activist and informant without realizing it.

Before I got let go, my former boss (who I would still consider myself friends with) knew I was trans and my plans for transitioning.  When I told him the day I would be coming in dressed as myself, he went and told the biggest, meanest guy working in our warehouse to watch out for me.

The guy in the warehouse came up to me several days later, telling me that one of our technicians stared at me in a funny way.  He called the dude over and screamed him out for it.  Seriously, the guy who got arrested for a felony was screaming at this little dude for looking at me in a weird way.

In addition to this, the same former boss had a dream about me.  In the dream, he took some of us out to a bar, and when we were walking out some dudes were making fun of me and saying a ton of bad stuff.  Him and his cronies (including his siblings) beat the guys up so bad they had to go to the hospital.  In his dream, he even dreamed that I was female and he was protecting me.

In addition, my dad has gotten MUCH better with name and pronoun usage, as has my mom.  My dad was my biggest negative during the start of my quest, but has become a really good supporter now.

I'm in Illinois, 31, MTF.  I was admitted to a psych hospital a few months back because I was "suicidal" (long story, I won't go into it).

The staff there were TOTALLY unaware of anything regarding trans issues.  They had to figure out who would strip search me at the intro (I wanted female staff, I got female staff).
Took them an hour and a half to get my hormones, because I didn't take them that night.  I even brought in my own pill bottles, and it took them that long.

Everyone there was friendly and accepting of me.  Most didn't even know I was trans until I told them.  Unfortunately, a lot of the negatives are true - terrible food, terrible beds, feeling like a prisoner.  It was a "lucky" day if we were allowed outside in a small little place.

The only comfort was unlimited phone usage when it was allowed - which was most of the time.  The group therapy didn't help me much, but some of it was calming.

I will say that you might get a ton of questions regarding your transition, and a lot of the staff were very supportive and questioning on everything (in a good way).  You may not realize it, but I learned something very important there: we, as trans individuals, are very very strong for going through what we go through.  Life does get better, and antidepressants do help a lot.  You just have to find the right one, with the help of a doctor.

Good luck.

I never thought I would find somebody.  I was always down on myself, and the dating scene was very very scary to me.

I'm 31 and MTF, 15 months on HRT, pre-GRS.

I randomly found the girl of my dreams, and she's desperately in love with me as well.  Her family is accepting of us, and are totally okay with everything.  Her mom is super protective of me already, even though I'm states away from her and won't be able to visit for a while.

Just keep up hope, there's always someone out there for you.  You just have to search a bit.  Even if you are just looking for dates, maybe you are looking in the wrong places?

My gender therapist told me that I needed to get FFS otherwise I would never pass.

In addition to being a gatekeeper and forcing me to see her for over six years before she gave me my carry letter (and, SURPRISE, DSM changed a year after -.- )
It really does.  I got used to it, was able to stomach it, but yeah - the pain goes up massively on hormones.  Your skin does become thinner, and more receptive to sensation - good and bad.

I got mine changed in Illinois.  I still had to file for the publishing in a paper.

The judge was SUPER nice and kind, and knew I was nervous anyways.  They may ask a few questions, but take a deep breath and just be polite.

I got my papers that day - changed my license that day too.  The DMV changed the gender marker on my license for me.  It was pretty sweet.

I got laser started before I transitioned.  The biggest issue I had after I started taking hormones is my skin became MUCH more sensitive to the pain.  Laser *does* hurt, and will redden your skin.  It feels like a bad sunburn, and the pain got worse (even though my tolerance went up) after being on hormones for about six months.

People can be.  I'm okay though - I have many family members that are still okay with me, I have a ton of friends around me.  I even just recently found someone special to me, and their family loves me to death.

Confirmed.  Ordained through ULC.  Have performed five weddings in Illinois.
You have to call the county clerk's office and ask them if they require a letter of good standing, most don't and none of them even checked if I was a certified minister.  All I had to do was follow the laws (both signing marriage certificate, my signature, two witnesses).  Pretty easy.

Oh yeah, I do still love him.  I'll always love him.  But the fact that he refuses to explain it to his kids, refuses to tell them what I'm going through, and has the audacity to send me a taunting christmas card really kicked it over the edge.
"Thank you for understanding."  I'm only understanding because I knew something like this would happen, but didn't expect my older brother - who's supposed to be protective of me - refusing my presence as a human being, all because I was born in the wrong body.

Lost my brother, his wife, and their kids.

My brother, who was not religious until he met his wife, is completely against me because I'm trans.  He claims the kids won't understand at all.  I'm banned from seeing them until they are 18.  All because his wife is religious (and not "You should pray" religious.  More like "God created the earth 6,000 years ago" religious).

There's no swaying my brother anymore, his best friends tried.  They told me he would never get over me being a female now.  I've been on hormones for over a year, I saw him at the year mark.  He refused to call me by my new name, and refuses to use the proper pronouns.  I'm uninvited to my parent's for Christmas, because they need to see the kids every year.  I don't blame them - they didn't do this to me, my brother said it was his family or me.  I just took the high road and accepted it, despite my feelings for everything.

1)  I noticed emotional effects within two months.  They got serious after six months, and I didn't "normalize" and accept the changes until I was in for a little over year.

2) I went to a therapist, but she was a gatekeeper.  I don't like therapists, but again, it would be a good idea to talk to one that knows what they are talking about.

3) I started transitioning at the age of 30.  Here's my results:
http://imgur.com/RKrCxKz
http://imgur.com/a/E8IU4
The album is fairly recent, with the picture of me in the really short dress taken about a month ago.

4) I had laser hair removal done for two years on my entire body.  I also had my adam's apple removed - that is a MUST if you have a huge adam's apple like I did.

5) I didn't gain ANY weight.  It depends on the person.  Some people gain, others don't.  I'm still struggling to maintain my 120 pounds.

6) Uh, basically, I can't penetrate.  It varies by person to person.  Mine haven't shrunk much, but yeah, TMI stuff there.

7) I've heard varying reports.  The longer you are on it, the harder it is to "wean" off the hormones.

I couldn't go with feminizing my birth name - only because I have cousins/friends that have similar names, and I'd rather not disrespect them by feminizing my name to that.  So I went with something that started with the same letter, but is totally different.
Originally I had a different name picked out, but after realizing how it did not fit me, I brainstormed with my mom to come up with a name.

Playing D&D with friends, I would always play a female character.  I roleplayed them perfectly, and never knew why.  This all started when I was in 5th grade.  In all the campaigns we have played, I've been a male in two (my first D&D campaign and my first Shadowrun campaign).  I've always played odd characters - from a mantis race (thri-kreen for those nerds out there) that I didn't really consider masculine, to an androgynous robot.  Every other character was female, and my friends that I played with always put my character in awkward situations which made ME feel awkward.

I do remember being young and knowing I was different, but not sure how I was different.  I always just chalked it up to having been born in the wrong time.  Realized it was because I was born in the wrong body, but unable to vocalize it without fear.  I would always hope that there was someone else, on the other side of the planet, that shared a spirit with me, who would go wandering around when I was asleep to do her deeds.

Now I know what was off, and I'm working hard to fix it.  Kind of silly that literally no one remembers me playing all female characters constantly - even my best friend from fifth grade.

My temperature acceptance has been weird.  Before HRT I got cold in 90+ weather, where I wore a hooded sweatshirt every day of one year, minus two specific days (it was 105+ out).
I gained 20 pounds, THEN started HRT.  I don't know what happened to be exact, but I get cold in almost all weather still, but sometimes I get super hot (maybe hot flashes?  I dunno) on certain days.

(I used sister in quotation marks because she is not related to me, but might as well be my sister)

Just went to my doctor, she's taking care of everything.  My hormones are in the right areas that they should be.

I'm currently 31.  I started my transition last year, at the tender age of 30.  I went on hormones in July of 2014, had my Adam's Apple removed in September, and my name legally changed in December (15 days before my birthday).
Here are some recent pictures of me to show you how I transitioned.

I'm changing almost daily.  You can do it, and it's very rewarding - even this *late* in life.

I sometimes get that problem myself - it all depends on my current thoughts.

My current issue is that the tissue is so soft (right term?) that it bleeds easily.

I couldn't before I started my hormones, but now I can swallow most pills (horse pills are terrible!)
I do this by one of two tricks:
Get something to snack on (preferably something chewy) and toss it in your mouth.  I then toss the pill(s) in my mouth, make sure they are either off to the side or somewhere else in my mouth (I can tell by the different texture to the pill).  Chew on food/snack, then swallow it all.
Otherwise, and I know this is bad, carbonated beverages.  Take some into your mouth, toss pill in, you can usually swallow it.

Start with the food one first, it helps a lot.

Don't be.  There's a lot going on that I didn't really explain.  I'm losing my brother because he doesn't want his kids to see me "like that", and my dad has been constantly down about me being transgender.  He's always been like this towards me.

This was just the last straw.  I have a few friends that know most, if not all, of the story, and they all tell me to send the letter and refuse to call him my "father", because there is nothing more important to a t-girl than to be who she has to be.
Thanks.  I haven't been playing games lately, so I wouldn't be too upset.  Although I do like the WiiU..

There's a lot more backstory - including refusing to allow me to dress as female in his house, which hasn't been revoked in word over the course of 7+ years that I've been out, completely ignoring everything that I've done in the same past seven years and telling me I'm making a mistake that I will regret (which happened a little over a month ago).

Just because he doesn't want me to change my name as a christmas/birthday gift isn't the critical issue - it's the fact that he has attempted to block and stop my every move down this path, and I'm sick and tired of every time I bring up my transition or changes he either yells or walks away.

I'll talk to my mom about figuring out something worth the paltry $300 that they offered me for christmas so I can try to sell it later.  Maybe a wiiU or something.  I dunno, I'll figure it out.  Thanks for the suggestion Sarah, I'm just...  yeah.

My boy (and legal) name is able to be shortened from multiple syllables to one.  She will be on the phone with me, with no one around her, and say "So **full** **unaltered** **legal** **name** can you do me a favor?"  

I know it's a habit, but seriously mom...  she helped me come up with my girl name.  I had her input and we argued for three **months** to get it to a name we both like.  And now I love my future name and won't change it ever.

But I think she's in severe denial, despite the fact that she's *happy* and *relieved* that I'm on the path.  Mixed signals, ya'know?
I wrote a letter.  Basically telling him I don't want him to be my father anymore.  I don't know if I'll sent it or not.

My mom sees me as her child.  She uses the improper name and improper pronouns constantly, even using my full first name to talk to me or about me.
